# CONFORMANCE

The conformance ID register. Every test name ends in its ID; a test whose
ID is not listed here fails `cargo xtask check-model`, and so does an ID
listed here with no scenario and no test (`CM-02`).

The three honesty levels (R2):

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `some-true` | A fact reproduced from an authority. **Not established here.** |
| `build` | Constructed here and validated against its oracle. Evidence, not a proof. |
| `open` | Measured and reported. **Never asserted.** |

`cargo xtask audit-limits` fails if any code path returns an error the
model does not sanction.

## attestation

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AT-01` | `build` | lexlean_attestation by attestation ID returns the signed envelope: for the record of a concluded verification the tool asks attestation.lookup once and answers found true with the envelope as its text, byte for byte the envelope in the store, and those bytes validate against keys/history and the stored attestation.json. |
| `AT-02` | `build` | lexlean_attestation by the SHA-256 of a source file that the verification covered returns the same envelope as by the attestation ID. |
| `AT-03` | `build` | A lookup that finds nothing is not an error and a malformed value is refused: an attestation ID or a digest that names no record, and an empty store, answer found false with the text not found; a value that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits is the host's refusal value-refused; an empty value is refused by the core as bad arguments and the host is not asked. |
| `AT-04` | `build` | A lookup writes nothing: the store holds the same files with the same bytes after lookups that find, that miss and that are refused. |
| `AT-05` | `build` | Each gate of the tool rejects its planted defect: the lookup reading the file that the envelope signs instead of the envelope, the digest read as an attestation ID, the check of the value dropped, and a lookup that writes to the store; ATTESTATION.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |

## signing

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SG-01` | `build` | The signer writes the DSSE envelope of a verification: the payload type is application/vnd.in-toto+json, the payload is the base64 of an in-toto Statement v1 whose one subject is attestation.json with the SHA-256 of the bytes the signer was given and whose predicate type is https://uor.foundation/lexlean-mcp/verification/v1 with the predicate the caller supplied, and there is one signature, whose keyid is the SHA-256 in hexadecimal of the public key and whose sig is the Ed25519 signature over PAE(payloadType, payload). |
| `SG-02` | `build` | The primitives are the standards': PAE reproduces the example of the DSSE protocol (DSSEv1 29 http://example.com/HelloWorld 11 hello world), the Ed25519 key that the signer derives from the seed of RFC 8032 section 7.1 test 1 has that test's public key and signs that test's empty message with that test's signature, and two envelopes made from equal inputs are equal to the byte because Ed25519 is deterministic. |
| `SG-03` | `build` | validate accepts the envelope the signer wrote, given a key history that holds its key and the bytes of the subject, and returns the statement: it checks the signature with the key the history names by the keyid (strict verification), the payload type, the statement type, the predicate type and that the subject digest is the SHA-256 of the bytes it was given. |
| `SG-04` | `build` | Every refusal of an envelope is typed and has a negative test: the constructors of EnvelopeError (Malformed, PayloadType, Payload, Statement, NoSignature, UnknownKey, BadSignature, KeyRevoked, SubjectMismatch) are each reached by a planted envelope --- not JSON, a payload type changed, a payload that is not base64, a statement of another type or predicate, no signatures, a keyid the history lacks, a flipped signature byte or payload byte, a revoked key and a subject of other bytes --- and none of them is accepted. |
| `SG-05` | `build` | The key history is appended by the signer and read back: the first signature with a key adds {keyid, algorithm Ed25519, public_key, not_before}, further signatures with it add nothing, a second key adds its own entry and the envelopes of the first still validate (rotation), revoke sets revoked_at so that the envelopes of that key fail with KeyRevoked while those of the other key still validate and the revoked key itself signs nothing (SignError::KeyRevoked), and a history that is not a list of well-formed entries is refused with HistoryError::Malformed. |
| `SG-06` | `build` | The key is a file secret: Signer::load reads 64 hexadecimal digits, with surrounding whitespace allowed, as the Ed25519 seed; a missing file is KeyError::Missing, an unreadable one KeyError::Unreadable and a file of any other content KeyError::Malformed; and neither the seed nor any part of it appears in the Debug output of the signer or of a KeyError, in an envelope or in the history. |
| `SG-07` | `build` | A signature that cannot be recorded is not returned: when the history cannot be written, sign returns SignError::History and no envelope; the history is written to a temporary file and renamed over the old one, so a reader sees the old list or the new one and no partial list, and no temporary file is left after a success. |
| `SG-08` | `build` | Each gate of the signer rejects its planted defect: the lengths of PAE swapped, the keyid taken from the seed instead of the public key, the digest of the subject not checked, a revoked key accepted, and the history not appended on the first use of a key; SIGNING.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |
| `SG-09` | `build` | The signing key is configured by the operator and a verification is not started without it: the host reads the path of the key file from LEXLEAN_MCP_SIGNING_KEY (an empty value is no path), keeps its history in the keys area of the store, and verify.start fails with verifier-unavailable, starts no task, runs no verification and leaves nothing in the builds area when no key is configured and when the configured file is missing, unreadable or malformed, while a project that is not one is refused as project-refused whatever the state of the key. |
| `SG-10` | `build` | A verification that ends verified leaves a record that is a signed envelope: verifications/<attestation ID>.json is the DSSE envelope, verifications/<attestation ID>/attestation.json is the attestation.json of the verified directory byte for byte, the envelope validates against keys/history with those bytes, its predicate carries the attestation, build, source and semantic IDs, the status verified, the modules and the SHA-256 of each source file, and the result of the task names the key. |
| `SG-11` | `build` | attestation.lookup returns the signed envelope: by attestation ID and by the SHA-256 of a source file the verification covered, the lookup of a concluded verification returns exactly the bytes of the envelope in the store, and those bytes validate against keys/history and the stored attestation.json. |
| `SG-12` | `build` | A verification that cannot be signed leaves no record: when the key's history cannot be written, or the attestation.json of the verified directory cannot be read, the task ends failed with class 5, and the store holds no envelope, no attestation.json and no index entry for it; a verification that failed leaves none either. |
| `SG-13` | `build` | Each gate of the signed record rejects its planted defect: verify.start accepting a verification without a key, the failure to sign ignored and an unsigned record written, the envelope stored without its attestation.json, the predicate without the digests of the source files, and the lookup answering the unsigned record again; SIGNING.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |
| `SG-14` | `build` | A verified record keeps the evidence its attestation.json binds: below verifications/<attestation ID>/ the store holds build-manifest.json, the manifest whose SHA-256 attestation.json names as build_manifest, each output of kind tex that the manifest names (the canonical LaTeX of a module) at its path, and each input of kind source at sources/<its path>, every file byte for byte with the digest the manifest gives, written after attestation.json and before the envelope; a real verification of the tiny project leaves such a record. |
| `SG-15` | `build` | A verification whose evidence cannot be kept whole leaves no record: when the build manifest is missing or is not the one attestation.json names, attestation.json names no manifest, a rendering or a source file is missing or differs from the digest the manifest gives, the manifest names no rendering or no source, or a path the manifest names is not a key of the store, the task ends failed with class 5 and the store holds no envelope, no attestation.json, no evidence, no index entry and no key entry for it. |

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ST-01` | `build` | The store layout of lexlean-mcp/store/1 is a closed type of seven directories, profiles, drafts, builds, verifications, index, exports and keys, in that order: each has one distinct wire name, every directory is listed, every wire name parses back to its directory and an unknown name is refused. |

| `ST-03` | `build` | Retention is a total function of the bound owner values: an attestation record never expires at any age, a draft record expires after store.draft_retention (30 days) and not before, and both durations are the values bound in src/OwnerValues.lex.tex. |
| `ST-04` | `build` | The drift check is a total function from the stored profile record, the lock check result, the recomputed profile ID and the recomputed toolchain hashes to one of NoDrift, LockDrift, IdDrift and ToolchainDrift, deciding in that order of precedence: lock, then ID, then toolchain; all eight inputs of the decision are tabulated, and a recomputation that Identity refuses is IdDrift. |
| `ST-05` | `build` | The lifecycle is a state machine over the served revision, the served profile set, the previous release, the retired profiles and the records: rollout, rollback, upgrade and retirement keep every record, rollback restores the previous revision and served set, an upgrade serves the new profile and a retired profile is not served. |
| `ST-06` | `build` | AC-14 (model): the profile preimage determines its toolchain field for every input, so a new LexLean revision gives another preimage, and after an upgrade the earlier records still resolve and still validate; this is a claim about preimages, not about SHA-256. |
| `ST-07` | `build` | AC-15 and AC-17 (model): returning to the previous revision serves its profiles and its revision, a record written after the rollout still resolves after the rollback, and a release rollback resolves every record that resolved before it. |
| `ST-08` | `build` | AC-16 (model): after restore from a backup every backed-up record resolves as before, the keys and the draft references are restored, and re-verifying a restored record yields the attestation ID it is stored under because the ID is a function of the profile and the inputs; the signed attestation format stays abstract until #11. |
| `ST-09` | `build` | Each law of the store model rejects its planted defect: an attestation that expires, a drift check that reports ToolchainDrift before IdDrift, a rollback that drops a later record and a restore that omits keys each fail lexlean verify; STORE.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |

| `TH-02` | `build` | clock.now answers a millisecond counter that never goes back and the same instant as ISO 8601 text in UTC with three digits of milliseconds: the text of 0 is 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, of 1700000000123 is 2023-11-14T22:13:20.123Z, of 951782400000 is 2000-02-29T00:00:00.000Z and of 1709164799999 is 2024-02-28T23:59:59.999Z, and the text of a later answer is the text of the start of the host plus the difference of the counters. |
| `TH-03` | `build` | task.id answers 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits, a different value at every call and at every host, made from the operating system's source of randomness and not from the clock or from a counter, so that no client can guess the identifier of a task it did not create. |
| `TH-04` | `build` | task.table answers the bytes that the last task.store gave and nothing before any: a store replaces the whole table, the host hands back exactly what it was given byte for byte, bytes of every value and a table of the 524296 bytes that the declaration allows included, and a store of an empty table empties it. |
| `TH-05` | `build` | The production core serves the vectors at the pin of MCP with the new frame: every request of gateway/vectors/exchanges.json is answered with the response recorded for it by the core of this commit, the adapter asks for the three frame effects of the time, the identifier and the table once for each request that reaches the core, and an exchange that creates or touches no task asks the core for no task.store. |
| `TH-06` | `build` | Each gate of the task host rejects its planted defect: the text of the time disagreeing with its counter, an identifier made from the counter, a store that appends to the table instead of replacing it, and a provider that names the wrong tag for the store; TASKHOST.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |
| `TH-07` | `build` | lexlean_verify called by a client that declares the tasks extension creates a task: the core asks verify.start as before, and when the host has started the verification the result is a task handle whose taskId is the task name the verifier gave, in the status working, with a time to live of 86400000 ms and a poll interval of 5000 ms, and the core asks task.store with a table that holds the task as working; a client that does not declare the extension is answered as before, with the task name in the result of the call and no task.store, and a verification that the host refuses to start creates no task. |
| `TH-08` | `build` | tasks/get on a task the table holds as working asks verify.control once for its status and settles the entry from the answer: queued and running leave it working with no notification, verified and failed complete it with the result of the tool, cancelled cancels it, and a verifier that no longer knows the task fails it with the code -32603; each answer about a task is followed by task.store with the table, and a notification of the new status is streamed before the response only when the task changed; a task that is already terminal is answered from the table without asking verify.control, and a task the table does not hold is the protocol's unknown task. |
| `TH-09` | `build` | tasks/cancel on a working task asks verify.control to cancel it, answers with the empty acknowledgement, streams a notification of the status cancelled and stores the task as cancelled; asked again, or on a task that is already terminal, it is answered from the table without asking verify.control, and on a task the table does not hold it is the protocol's unknown task. |
| `TH-10` | `build` | A cancel says what became of the child groups (AC-12): tasks/cancel on a working task settles it with the status message child groups ended: E failed: F, the counts that verify.control gave, which the status notification, a later tasks/get and the table all carry, so a cancel with a group that failed to end is not reported as a clean one. |
| `TH-11` | `build` | The task path runs with the real verifier and the Lean toolchain: lexlean_verify by a client that declares the tasks extension, polled with tasks/get, ends completed with the state verified, and its record is found by its ID and validates; tasks/cancel while a program of the toolchain runs reports at least one child group ended and none failed, and leaves no record. |

## tools

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TL-01` | `build` | The tools of F4 to F7 declare one schema each: lexlean_check, lexlean_snapshot, lexlean_format and lexlean_build take project (a non-empty string), files (strings) and all (a boolean), lexlean_format also check_only, and no other member; each declares an outputSchema, the lexlean/command-result/1 object for check, format and build and an object with a spec for snapshot; tools/list through the production core shows exactly these, and a call whose arguments break the schema is refused by the core as an Invalid arguments error result before any effect is asked for, while a call the schema admits and the tool cannot make (all together with files, a file name with a line feed) is the protocol error invalid params, and neither is ever an answer of the Engine. |
| `TL-02` | `build` | An answer of the Engine is a tool result and never a protocol error: class 0 gives a result without isError whose structuredContent is the canonical command result, classes 1, 2 and 4 give isError true with the command result of the failure, the text block is the same JSON, a host failure (project-refused, engine-unavailable) gives isError true with its failure name, and bytes that are not a command result or whose exit_code differs from the class are a typed internal refusal of the core. |
| `TL-03` | `build` | AC-07: for every check fixture that issue #10 puts in F4 and for the build fixture of F7 in tests/negative of the LexLean commit of gateway/mcp/lexlean.rev, lexlean_check and lexlean_build give what lexlean --diagnostic-format json check and build give for the same project: the same exit code and class, the same diagnostics, the same bytes in the text block, and the same files in the project afterwards; the test runs the CLI and the tool, and the fixtures it runs are the F4 and F7 rows of the register plus the names the register lacks. |
| `TL-04` | `build` | lexlean_snapshot on the same fixtures agrees with the CLI: a refused project gives the command result that lexlean check gives with command snapshot, an accepted one gives a semantic snapshot whose source_id and semantic_id are those lexlean check prints, and the bytes of the result are the canonical bytes of the Engine's snapshot. |
| `TL-05` | `build` | lexlean_format agrees with lexlean fmt: on the same fixtures check_only true gives the result of lexlean fmt --check and writes nothing, and check_only false gives the result of lexlean fmt and leaves the project with the same files, byte for byte. |
| `TL-06` | `build` | AC-04: each project of examples/ of the LexLean commit of gateway/mcp/lexlean.rev, with its configuration, lock, local packages and artifact sources, builds through lexlean_build to the tree of its expected/ directory byte for byte (the process-bound files by presence), and the build is the one lexlean build makes. |
| `TL-07` | `build` | AC-08: a draft with an atom outside the profile gives, through lexlean_check, an isError result with the diagnostic LLL1004 and its span (path, byte range, line and column), the same as the CLI gives. |
| `TL-08` | `build` | Q4: lexlean_check, lexlean_snapshot, lexlean_format and lexlean_build start no child process: the host process accounting (the waited-for children of /proc/self/stat and the live children of every thread) does not move across a call of each, in a test binary in which nothing else spawns, and the same instrument sees a child that a control spawns. |
| `TL-09` | `build` | Each gate of the tools rejects its planted defect: a class mapped to the wrong exit code, a diagnostic dropped from a result, and a format whose bytes differ from the CLI's; TOOLS.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |
| `TL-10` | `build` | lexlean_explain (F11) is declared with one input, code (a string, any string), no other member, and an outputSchema that is the lexlean/command-result/1 object with command explain; tools/list through the production core shows it; a call to it asks the host for no effect, because an explanation is a pure function of the code that is compiled into the core, so src/Effects.lex.tex and the set E1 to E10 do not change; and a call that breaks the schema is refused by the core as an Invalid arguments error result before the tool runs. |
| `TL-11` | `build` | The explanations compiled into the core are the rendering of the registry: gateway/src/Explain.lex.tex is what gateway/explain/generate.py renders from model/errors.toml of the LexLean commit of gateway/mcp/lexlean.rev, with one entry for every registered code and none other, the gateway job fails when the committed module is not that rendering, and the tool layer holds no explanation text of its own. |
| `TL-12` | `build` | For every code that the registry of the LexLean commit of gateway/mcp/lexlean.rev registers, lexlean_explain gives what lexlean --diagnostic-format json explain gives: a result without isError whose text is the CLI's standard output byte for byte and whose structuredContent is its parse; and for every string the registry does not register (the empty string, a code in another case, quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII, a code that begins with a dash, which the CLI reads after --) it gives the CLI's refusal: isError true, exit_code 2, the diagnostic LLC0001 that quotes the string, the same bytes; the codes are read from the registry and not typed, and their count is asserted. |
| `TL-13` | `build` | Q8, the running clause: every diagnostic code that appears in the result of lexlean_check or lexlean_build on the fixtures of TL-03 resolves through lexlean_explain to the entry the CLI prints for it, and the test counts the distinct codes it resolved. |
| `TL-14` | `build` | Each gate of lexlean_explain rejects its planted defect: a wrong byte in an explanation, an unregistered code answered as registered, and an unknown code quoted with an escape that differs from the CLI's; TOOLS.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |
| `TL-15` | `build` | Q2, the running clause: each of the nine in-scope functions of crates/quality-map/map.toml is reached by a tool that tools/list of the production core shows and that runs, lexlean_check, lexlean_snapshot, lexlean_format, lexlean_build and lexlean_verify for the Engine calls, and lexlean_draft_assemble and lexlean_draft_read for sdk::assemble, sdk::write_module, sdk::read_module and sdk::declaration_spans, whose results equal what those functions give on the same text. |

## verifier

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VP-01` | `build` | The verifier is a program that speaks lines of JSON: gateway-verifier becomes the leader of a session of its own and says so in a started event that names the session, reads one job line (the directory of the project and the selection) from its standard input, runs Engine::verify and prints one verdict --- verified with the IDs, the modules and the verified directory, failed with the class and the diagnostics of the engine, or cancelled with the groups it ended and those it could not end --- on a line of its standard output; a line cancel on its standard input ends every live child group of the process, the end of that input ends them and the process, and a job line that is not a job is a failed verdict of class 5. |
| `VP-02` | `build` | Each task runs in a process of its own that does not hold the key: verify.start starts the program of the configuration (LEXLEAN_MCP_VERIFIER, else gateway-verifier beside the running executable) with the width and the memory of the owner values in LEXLEAN_VERIFY_WIDTH and LEXLEAN_VERIFY_MEMORY_KIB, without LEXLEAN_MCP_SIGNING_KEY in its environment and with nothing of the seed or of the path of the key file in its arguments, its environment or its input; when the configured program is not a file, verify.start fails with verifier-unavailable, starts no task and leaves nothing in the builds area. |
| `VP-03` | `build` | The tasks run as many at a time as the slots of verify.concurrency allow and the others wait: with one slot the second and the third of three tasks are Queued while the first runs, none fails for waiting, they run in the order they were started and never two at once; with two slots two run at once; and a verification that the process reports verified is signed and recorded by the host with the facts the process printed, in the process of the host. |
| `VP-04` | `build` | A cancel ends one task: a queued task leaves the queue and its process is never started; a running task is sent cancel, the answer carries the groups its process reported, the task ends Cancelled with no record and the other tasks are not touched; a process that reports verified while the cancel is pending leaves no record, because the record is made under the lock that the cancel takes; and a process that does not answer within the grace is killed, together with its session. |
| `VP-05` | `build` | A verifier that is lost leaves nothing: a process that ends without a verdict, by exiting or by a signal, ends its task Failed with class 5 and the result {"failure":"verifier-lost"} with the tail of its standard error, no record is made, the other tasks are not touched, and every process left in its session --- children that outlived it --- is killed, because LexLean starts its own children with an empty environment, so no marker in the environment can find them. |
| `VP-06` | `build` | Each gate of the verifier process rejects its planted defect: the key left in the environment of the process, a record made for a task that is being cancelled, the session of a lost verifier not killed, the slots ignored so that every task starts at once, and a process that ignores cancel left running; VERIFIER.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |

## vocabulary

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VO-01` | `build` | The profile ID that the host computes is Identity.profileId: the host's encoder reproduces the model's profilePreimageVector, profileIdVector and profileFramingReviewsVector byte for byte, gateway/vectors/generate.py computes the ID of the vectors' profile again in Python and the host agrees, and the toolchain of the preimage is the compiler-semantics ID and the Lean toolchain of the lock that lock --check has just accepted. |
| `VO-02` | `build` | Changing any file of a provisioned profile changes the profile ID the host records: a byte of lexlean.toml, of lexlean.lock, of a file of a local lexicon package or of an artifact_source file, a renamed profile file, an added one, a removed one and a review record each give another ID, while a file under a source root leaves it alone. |
| `VO-03` | `build` | The language rule of the gateway is the model's and not a second copy: gateway/src/ProfileLanguage.lex.tex holds PackageCheck, PackageDecl, languageMismatchCode, checkPackage and checkPackages byte for byte as src/Profiles.lex.tex declares them, the model carries them as executable, and a test compares the text of each declaration. |
| `VO-04` | `build` | A package of another language is refused with LLC0103 at every place it could enter: install refuses a project whose lexicon package has another language with the compiler's own LLC0103 and installs nothing, and a catalogue or a vocabulary that holds such a package is not served, lexlean_profiles lists the profile under refused with LLC0103 and not among profiles, lexlean_lexicon_search and the read of its resources are refused with LanguageMismatch and the code LLC0103, and none of its entries is returned. |
| `VO-05` | `build` | Provisioning is an operator command of the binding and not an effect: gateway-provision init and lock run lexlean init and lexlean lock in process, --allow-network is accepted by lock alone, install never writes the lock (a stale lock is the compiler's LLC0102 and a missing lock is refused), no tool of the gateway locks, initialises or installs, and the set of effects is still the model's ten. |
| `VO-06` | `build` | A package that enters from a path or from Git needs a review record before a profile is installed (K2, and the measurement of risk 2 that SECURITY.md executes): a record is four lines (lexlean-mcp-review-v1, package ID@VERSION, tree_sha256 and the digest, reviewer and a name), install refuses a locked path or Git package that no record names with ReviewMissing, a record that is not four such lines with ReviewMalformed, a record that names no locked package or another tree digest than the lock's with ReviewStale and a record given twice with ReviewDuplicate, a builtin package needs none, and the bytes of every record enter the profile ID and are stored as reviews/<SHA-256 of the record>. |
| `VO-07` | `build` | install lays out the profile as one rename into the profiles area and leaves the store as it was when it refuses: profiles/<name> holds the project as locked (not .git, .lake, or .lexlean but its Git package cache), the record profile, the derived vocabulary and the reviews, the catalogue index/profiles lists it, a name that is not a valid key segment is NameInvalid, a name already installed is ProfileExists, a project with a symbolic link is LinkInBundle, a top-level entry named profile, vocabulary or reviews is ReservedEntry, a project with source packages is SourcePackagesUnsupported, and materialization (DR-07) copies the bundle without the record, the vocabulary and the reviews. |
| `VO-08` | `build` | The vocabulary is the entries of the packages that the compiler resolved for the project, as lexlean::lock::resolve_packages loads them: the document lists each locked lexicon package with its version, its language and its number of entries, and the entries in package and local ID order each with its package, version, category, frame, arity, denotation and forms, an entry that denotes a module the source roots of the profile lack is left out, and a vocabulary over 1 MiB (the bound of lexicon.read) is VocabularyTooLarge. |
| `VO-09` | `build` | lexlean_profiles takes an optional profile and asks one store.get of the key profiles of the index area: it answers every installed profile with its name, ID, language, source roots and packages (package, version, language, entries), a named profile that is not installed is ProfileUnknown, a catalogue that is not the layout is CatalogueMalformed, a profile whose packages are not all of its language is under refused with the code LLC0103, an absent catalogue is no profile, and the input schema is closed. |
| `VO-10` | `build` | lexlean_lexicon_search takes a profile, an optional query (matched against the entry ID and the spelling of every form without regard to ASCII case), an optional package, an offset and a limit of at most 100, asks one lexicon.read of the entry vocabulary and answers total, offset and the entries of the page in vocabulary order; an unknown profile is the host failure profile-unknown, a profile without a vocabulary is VocabularyMissing, a vocabulary that is not the layout is VocabularyMalformed, and the input schema is closed. |
| `VO-11` | `build` | The resource template lexlean://profiles/{profile}/lexicon/{package}@{version} is served with cacheScope public and the owner's cache.ttl_ms: resources/templates/list answers it with no effect, resources/list answers one resource for every package of every installed profile with one store.get, and resources/read of a URI of the template asks one lexicon.read of the vocabulary and answers the entries of that package as application/json text; a URI that is not of the template, a profile that is not installed and a package or version the profile lacks are the protocol error -32602 with the URI, and a package of another language is refused as in VO-04. |
| `VO-12` | `build` | completion/complete of the reference ref/resource of the template completes the argument profile from the installed profiles and the argument package from the packages of the profile that context.arguments.profile names (from all installed profiles when it names none), by prefix and at most 100 values with total and hasMore as MCP's Resources.completionOf computes them; another reference, another argument name and a profile that is not installed in the context are the protocol error -32602 or no value as stated by the tests, and the call asks one store.get. |
| `VO-13` | `build` | The capabilities the gateway declares are those it serves and no others: server/discover declares tools, resources and completions, a method of each is answered, prompts and the tasks methods are not declared and are answered as before, gateway/waiting.json names exactly the scenarios of MCP's server suite that still fail with a reason that is true of this gateway, and GATEWAY-CONFORMANCE.md is that table. |
| `VO-14` | `build` | An Atlas profile serves all 293 entries through the tools and the resource template: the project examples/uor-atlas of the pinned LexLean installs as a profile of language 1.0 with its 86 core modules in its source root, lexlean_profiles lists lexlean.uor.atlas 1.0.0 with 293 entries, lexlean_lexicon_search pages through exactly the 293 entry IDs of the model's atlasEntries, and resources/read of the Atlas package returns the same 293 entries; a profile without the module Atlas serves none of them. |
| `VO-15` | `build` | Every refusal of provisioning and of the vocabulary tools is typed and has a negative test: the constructors of provision::Refusal (NameInvalid, ProfileExists, ProjectUnreadable, Compiler, LinkInBundle, ReservedEntry, SourcePackagesUnsupported, ReviewMissing, ReviewMalformed, ReviewStale, ReviewDuplicate, VocabularyTooLarge, IdentityRefused, StoreUnwritable), the tool refusals ProfileUnknown, CatalogueMalformed, VocabularyMissing, VocabularyMalformed and LanguageMismatch, the host failures profile-unknown and key-refused of lexicon.read, the invalid arguments of the two tools, and the protocol error -32602 of a resource that is not found and of a completion that is not served. |
| `VO-16` | `build` | Each gate of the profile work rejects its planted defect: a profile file excluded from the identity, a mixed-language package admitted, an Atlas entry missing from the served lexicon, a capability declared that is not served, a profile installed without a review record and a reserved entry copied into a project; PROFILES.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |
